title: Fill a tax bracket with a Roth conversion and see the tax impact
summary: Add a Roth conversion that fills a tax bracket in the Solver, then compare lifetime taxes and taxes at death with it on and off.

chapters.label: A Roth conversion can fill a low tax bracket before RMDs begin.
On the Techniques tab, add a Roth conversion.
Pick Fill Up Tax Bracket and choose the 22% bracket.
Convert Laura's 401(k) from her retirement in 2035 through 2044.
On Taxes, each orange bar tops out at the edge of the 22% bracket.
Four years of conversions move her whole 401(k) into her Roth.
On Portfolio, lifetime taxes fall compared with the base plan.
Switch the conversion off, and the tax savings disappear.
Switch it back on to keep it in the plan.
On Estate, compare base facts with the plan at the second death.
Heirs inherit a Roth, so far less is lost to income tax.
Off, the two plans match. On, the savings return.

steps: **Add a Roth conversion.** In the Solver, open the **Techniques** tab and select **Roth conversion**.
**Choose the bracket.** Name the conversion, select **Fill Up Tax Bracket**, and pick the bracket in **Fill Up To**.
**Set the years and the account.** Choose when it **Starts** and **Ends**, then add the pre-tax account under **Accounts to Convert**. Select **Add Conversion**.
**Check the Taxes view.** Orange bars show each year's conversion on top of the household's other taxable income. They stop at the edge of the bracket you chose.
**Compare lifetime taxes.** On **Portfolio**, **Lifetime Taxes** shows the change from the base plan. Use the switch on the conversion's row to turn it off and on.

**Compare the estate.** On **Estate**, the chart sets **Base Facts** beside the plan at the second death. **Total Taxes & Expenses** includes the income tax heirs owe on inherited pre-tax accounts, so a converted account shrinks it.
goodToKnow: A conversion can only go into a Roth owned by the same person, so **Accounts to Convert** lists only that person's pre-tax accounts. **+ New Roth IRA** adds one if they don't have a Roth yet.
Conversions stop once the source accounts are empty, which can be before the **Ends** year.
The conversion stays in the Solver until you save it as a scenario or to base facts.
